messages.subject: Plotting ribbons around a line
parts:
I'm trying to plot a time series line from one dataset (a time series with one y per x), and a summary ribbon from a different dataset in the background (a time series with multiple y's per each x). 

The look and feel of fig 5.17 from the book is sort of what I'm after. My problem is the code that produces a plot produces very funky looking ribbon polygons. I can't tell if it's because of the shape of the ribbon (i.e. multiple crossing ymin and ymax, etc.), or a problem in my code.

Here's what I have using pointrange that currently works (and the plot it produces):

roms.v <- ggplot(data=tube, aes(as.Date(LocDateTime), ROMS_temp)) +  stat_summary(fun.data = "median_hilow", geom = "pointrange") + geom_line(aes(x=as.Date(LocDateTime), y=ROMS_temp), data=turtle, colour="red")


But calling geom_ribbon():


roms.v <- ggplot(data=tube, aes(as.Date(LocDateTime), ROMS_temp)) +   geom_line(aes(x=as.Date(LocDateTime), y=ROMS_temp), data=turtle, colour="red")+ stat_summary(geom="ribbon", fun.ymin="min", fun.ymax="max")


produces this plot with funky overlapping polygons.


Any suggestions on how to address this?


Cheers,

Rob


--
Robert S. Schick, Ph.D.
Duke University
